interface.signature: def solve(N: int, A: list[int], B: list[int]) -> int:

preconditions.description: Arrays A and B must have the same length N.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(x, int) for x in A) and all(isinstance(x, int) for x in B)
preconditions.description: All elements in A and B must be integers.

postconditions.expression: result == -1 or (all(A[i] + diffs[i] == B[i] for i in range(N)) and result >= 0)
postconditions.description: If result is not -1, then the transformed array A (after applying operations) must exactly match B, and the result must be a non-negative integer representing the minimum number of operations.

postconditions.expression: result == -1 or (all(diffs[i] >= 0 for i in range(N)) and all(diffs[i] == diffs[i-1] + (1 if i > 0 else 0) for i in range(1, N)) or all(diffs[i] == diffs[i+1] + (1 if i < N-1 else 0) for i in range(N-1)))
postconditions.description: If result is not -1, then the differences (B[i] - A[i]) must be non-negative and can be achieved by a sequence of prefix and suffix increments, meaning the differences must be non-decreasing or non-increasing in a way that allows prefix/suffix operations.

postconditions.expression: result == -1 or (all(B[i] >= A[i] for i in range(N)) and any(B[i] != A[i] for i in range(N)))
postconditions.description: If result is not -1, then every element in B must be greater than or equal to the corresponding element in A, and at least one element must differ (otherwise no operations are needed).
